summary: Describes using elliptic curve algorithms, ECDH with EnvelopedData and ECDSA with SignedData, to protect the AsymmetricKeyPackage content type in CMS. It extends RFC 5959 and is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo describes how existing elliptic-curve algorithms can protect CMS asymmetric key packages. ECDSA and ECDH are optional, but implementations that support either must support keys on the P-256 curve.

subtitle: Conventions for using ECDH and ECDSA with CMS asymmetric key packages.

tldr.problem: The CMS asymmetric key package conventions needed to cover elliptic-curve algorithms for signed and enveloped data.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC allows ECDSA with SignedData and standard ECDH with EnvelopedData, while requiring P-256 support when either is supported.
tldr.outcome: RFC 6162 extends RFC 5959 and defines no new algorithms.

facts.label: Required curve when using ECDH or ECDSA

today: RFC 6162 is a Proposed Standard and updates RFC 5959. The unit metadata records no RFC that obsoletes RFC 6162.

sections.title: Elliptic-Curve Algorithms for Key Packages
sections.content: RFC 6162 describes conventions for protecting the AsymmetricKeyPackage content type with Cryptographic Message Syntax (CMS). It amends RFC 5959 by extending the algorithms used with SignedData and EnvelopedData to include ECDSA and ECDH. The memo does not define new algorithms; it refers to previously defined ones.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo adds ways to use existing elliptic-curve algorithms with CMS key packages. It does not create new cryptographic algorithms.

sections.title: Signing and Key Agreement
sections.content: If an implementation supports SignedData, it MAY support ECDSA. When key agreement is used with EnvelopedData, an implementation MAY support standard ECDH rather than cofactor ECDH. Both choices are optional.
sections.plainLanguage: An implementation may use ECDSA to sign data and standard ECDH for key agreement. This memo does not require either algorithm.

sections.title: Required Curve Support
sections.content: The RFC says public-key certificates are the easiest way to implement SignedData and EnvelopedData. If an implementation supports ECDSA or ECDH, it MUST support keys on the P-256 curve.
sections.plainLanguage: ECDSA and ECDH are optional. If an implementation supports either, it must support P-256 keys.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The security considerations in the referenced certificate, CMS and elliptic-curve specifications apply to this document. RFC 6162 adds no separate security rules of its own.
sections.plainLanguage: Implementations should follow the security guidance in the related certificate, CMS and elliptic-curve specifications.
